title: Kushnarenkovo culture
fact_summary: An archaeological culture known from cemeteries in the Trans-Ural and Volga regions. Several genetic studies connect some of its cemeteries with the ancient Hungarians.

claims.text: Uyelgi, in the Trans-Ural region, is described as a cemetery of the late Kushnarenkovo culture, used from the end of the 8th to the 11th century.
Bolshie Tigani and Tankeevka in the Volga region are described as Kushnarenkovo/Karayakupovo culture mixed with early Bulgars.
A 2022 study reports long-lasting genetic connections between Kushnarenkovo sites and sites of the later Chiyalik culture.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: The Hungarians' homeland was probably in the southern Trans-Ural region, where the Kushnarenkovo culture spread.
claims.certainty_reason: One tier B study argues it.

open_questions.text: An archaeological culture is a style of objects and burials. Can it be matched to a language or a people?
